title: Wavefront FlashAttn Kernel Adapter: coalesced async pipeline and paged-KV hybrid prefetch
content:
Summary:

This note captures a design sketch and early microbench findings for a Wavefront FlashAttention kernel adapter that aims to: 1) enable lightweight coalesced fusion of FlashAttn + fused pointwise ops, 2) support an asynchronous prefetch pipeline tuned for paged KV caches, and 3) expose a scheduling hint interface to the runtime (wavefront priorities) without hard-coding policy. The adapter is intended as a thin layer between the serving runtime scheduler and device kernels so we can iterate on fusion heuristics and paged-KV prefetch policies independently.

Background and motivation:

We keep hitting two correlated pain points on 8x A100 stacks for long-context chat workloads: frequent tiny FlashAttn launches (high kernel launch overhead), and tail latency spikes when paged-KV faults happen mid-request. Existing monolithic fusion attempts reduce launch overhead but are brittle across model variants and sequence-length distributions. The adapter approach provides a protocol for coalescing logical ops at enqueue time and a small runtime-managed staging buffer for paged-KV prefetches.

Goals:
- Reduce per-token CPU+GPU overhead for short bursts (<= 32 tokens) by ~20–30% relative to current baseline microbatching.
- Eliminate >95th-percentile tail latency spikes due to on-demand KV page faults during decode.
- Allow operator-level tradeoffs (eagerness of fusion, prefetch distance) to be tuned per-customer/workload at runtime.

Design overview (high level):

1) Kernel adapter abstraction (wavefront-adapter):
   - API surface exposed to runtime (enqueue_kernel(op_descriptor, wave_meta)).
   - Enqueue is non-blocking; adapter groups descriptors into wavefronts for a short coalescing window (default 200us).
   - Adapter emits a single fused kernel launch for the wavefront, or multiple launches if resource constraints require splitting.

2) Fusion and coalescing heuristics:
   - Lightweight fusion: only fuse FlashAttn + immediately following pointwise ops (layernorm, linear residual add) when operand shapes and quantization profiles match.
   - Coalescing window collects same-model, same-layer ops from different requests (microbatch across logical requests) up to a max tokens threshold per-launch (configurable).
   - Cost model: estimate peak-SM occupancy and expected shared memory pressure; conservative fallback to unfused FlashAttn if occupancy < threshold.

3) Paged-KV hybrid prefetch pipeline:
   - Two-stage prefetch: (a) local per-GPU warm prefetch (synchronous prefetch of next N pages into device staging slab), (b) adapter-level async prefetch that issues DMA + host->device transfers ahead of fused kernel launches.
   - Prefetch distance is computed from observed token decode rate and historical page-access latency distribution; default target is to have KV pages resident 1–2 kernels ahead of demand.
   - Hybrid mode toggles between eager prefetch (higher memory, fewer faults) and opportunistic prefetch (lower memory, possible path to fast-fail fallback).

4) Eviction policy coupling:
   - Adapter exposes hint bits per-page: hot / warm / cold based on recency and wavefront frequency. Eviction favors cold pages and uses a tiny frequency sketch per-cohort.
   - On memory pressure, adapter tries to compact staging slab by merging small pages and evicting cold cohorts first. This minimizes fragmentation and DMA work.

Wavefront kernel adapter: implementation sketch:

- Data structures: ring of wavefront descriptors (flat structs), small per-GPU staging slab allocator (power-of-two buckets), page state table (resident, pending, faulted). Keep structures friendly to atomic ops to avoid global locks.

- Enqueue flow: runtime -> adapter.enqueue(op_desc):
  * validate shapes, tags
  * append to current wavefront slot
  * if coalescing window elapsed or tokens threshold reached -> build fused launch plan
  * schedule prefetches for any non-resident pages referenced by that wavefront
  * submit kernel(s) and attach completion callback that will update page frequency hints and metrics

- Launch planner: picks either fused FlashAttn kernel or fallback sequence of primitive ops. Planner uses a cheap heuristic + cached microbench stats keyed by (model, seq_len, dtype, cached_quant_profile).

Coalesced op fusion and warp-level handshake:

- Instead of a monolithic fusion compiled per-model, adapter uses a tiny warp-level handshake protocol embedded in the fused kernel header:
  * header contains an operation table, ranges for each request's tokens in the wavefront, and pointers to per-request NEON-like parameter blocks (scale, bias, residual pointers).
  * warps iterate over a combined token dimension; each warp reads a short 8-bit tag to decide which micro-op to run on a token, enabling per-token op variability with minimal branching.

- Benefit: supports heterogeneous microbatching where different requests in a wavefront may have different prompt prefixes and yet still be executed in a single launch. Overhead: ~2–4% extra memory per-token for tags; typically acceptable.

Async prefetch and backpressure model:

- Prefetch pipeline stages: page-resolve -> host-DMA -> device-staging -> kernel-ready. Each stage has a small credit pool to avoid over-committing PCIe bandwidth.
- Backpressure: if pipeline depth is exceeded for a GPU, adapter can either pause coalescing (emit smaller bursts) or downgrade to opportunistic prefetch and set wavefront priority low so scheduler favors other work.

Scheduling: wavefront priorities and soft preemptor:

- Wavefront meta includes priority hint (latency-critical, best-effort, background). Scheduler maps these to queue priorities and time-slices.
- Soft preemptor: a short-running watchdog that can trigger preemption between kernel launches (not within) by reordering pending wavefronts and, if necessary, issuing a light-weight abort + resubmit for long-running fused kernels. Use conservative thresholds because preemption in fused kernels has cost (KV state rollbacks).

Metrics and microbench results (early):

Testbed: 8x A100(40GB), model: Llama-2-13B-like transformer, dense QKV, seq len 4096, baseline runtime microbatch size=1 with current-pipeline.
- Baseline median decode p50 per-token GPU time: 1.6ms
- Adapter fused wavefront (200us window) median: 1.25ms (~22% improvement)
- 95th percentile baseline: 9.8ms (paged-KV fault dominated)
- 95th percentile adapter + hybrid prefetch: 2.1ms (major reduction in page-fault tail)
- Measured PCIe host->device transfer overlap: ~75% overlap when prefetch distance >=2 kernels ahead.

Notes on variance: wins are workload dependent. When request arrival jitter is very high and coalescing window yields only single-request wavefronts, fusion advantage vanishes and adapter falls back to microbatching heuristics.

Experiments run and observations:
- Experiment A: increase coalescing window 100us -> 500us. Observed: bigger windows yield small additional throughput but increase cold-start latency for very low QPS tenants. Tradeoff: dynamic windows by tenant class recommended.
- Experiment B: eager prefetch (N=4 pages) vs opportunistic (N=1): eager eliminated nearly all page faults at the cost of 6–8% higher resident memory on GPU.
- Experiment C: activate warp-tag per-token vs compile-time homogenous fusion: warp-tag version increased flexibility and supported heterogenous requests; measured overhead ~3% vs homogenous but saved separate kernel compilation complexity.

Risks and unknowns:
- Complexity: adapter increases code surface area; must be well tested to avoid regressions under failure (OOM, PCIe resets).
- Prefetch misprediction: bad prefetch distance selection could increase OOM churn and evictions, increasing overall latency.
- Preemption cost for fused kernels: abort+resubmit semantics are tricky if the kernel has mutated shared KV staging state. Need idempotent commit points or checkpointing.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define a compact per-wave metadata schema for tagging hot/warm/cold keys (8–16 bytes per key) and evaluate memory overhead.
- Evaluate impact on quantized kernels (4-bit) where additional decode cost might change fusion tradeoffs.
- Implement simple simulator for prefetch distance policy using historical page latency logs to tune default values per-region.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Stage 0 (2 weeks): prototype wavefront adapter scaffolding + ring descriptors + microbench harness.
- Stage 1 (4 weeks): implement simple fusion planner + fused FlashAttn launch with warp-tag support; unit tests.
- Stage 2 (4 weeks): implement paged-KV prefetch pipeline with host DMA credits and staging slab; integrate with eviction hints.
- Stage 3 (2 weeks): telemetry hooks, per-tenant config knobs (coalescing window, prefetch mode), gated rollout.

References and links:
- See linked PR for initial fused kernel prototype: https://git.company/repo/pulls/4583
- Jira ticket for paged-KV priority policy: ENG-1234
- Confluence: WavefrontKernelAdapterDraft

Appendix: quick pseudo-flow for enqueue (informal):

1) enqueue(op): store op_desc in current_wave
2) if current_wave.tokens + op.tokens > WAVE_MAX_TOKENS or now - wave_start > COALESCE_WINDOW -> plan_wave(current_wave)
3) plan_wave: identify missing pages -> issue async prefetch requests (respecting credit limits)
4) build fused launch payload (op table + per-request param blocks)
5) submit kernel and return a lightweight future to runtime

End of note.

Feedback welcome — particularly on the prefetch credit model and how conservative to be on coalescing window defaults.
